requirement:
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line containing its name; an anonymous node is declared on the
line where it starts. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the sources satisfy `requirements.cli.add_input_item`. The code is marked `{impl}`, the behavior matches the text, and the tests cover the interesting cases.

**Implementation**
- **CLI.** `src/main.rs` (`enum[Command]` / `AddInput`, and `main`) takes `--item <file>:<line>` as one of two exclusive modes and passes it to `add_input` as `InputMode::ItemsAtLine`.
- **Parsing and line parsing.** `selectors_for_mode` in `src/add_input.rs` splits the spec with `rsplit_once(':')`, so paths containing colons still work. It rejects a non-numeric line. It parses the file through `OutlineCache::parse`, which uses the outline profile chosen by file extension. That includes the plain-text profile, where each non-blank line is an anonymous `line` node (`plain_text` in `src/outline/mod.rs`).
- **Declared-on-line rule.** `Outline::declared_on_line` selects every non-root node whose `declaration_line` equals the requested line. The builder sets `declaration_line` to the line of the name for named nodes (`Builder::name` returns the name's start byte). For anonymous nodes it uses the line where the node starts, excluding attached docs and attributes (`walk` and `finish`). Several nodes on one line, such as `fn[main]` and `fn[main]/fn[nested]`, are all selected.
- **Rejection.** If nothing is selected, `selectors_for_mode` returns the error `<file>:<line>: no outline node is declared on this line`. Line 0 and blank lines are rejected the same way. The `?` operator aborts the command before the record is written.
- **Stored input.** `InputSelector::to_input` in `src/inputs.rs` stores exactly `file`, `item` (the selector) and `hash` (the node's structural hash), with no source text. `file` is recorded project-relative when inside the project (`strip_prefix(root)`). Otherwise it is the absolute resolved path, which matches the path rules in `requirements.ci.schema`. `resolve` checks containment through `read_project_file`.
- **Add, refresh, report.** `update_inputs` matches an existing input by selector. It then reports `added`, `refreshed` or `unchanged` for every selected node, followed by the selector. It leaves the record byte-identical when nothing changed.
- **Extra behavior.** `update_inputs` also resets `determination` to false and captures definition inputs when something changed. That behavior belongs to `requirements.cli.add_input` and `requirements.definitions.capture`, and the code carries `{impl}` markers for those.

**Tests** (`tests/commands.rs`)
- `add_input_modes_capture_outline_nodes_and_refresh_idempotently`:
  - Adding `src/main.rs:4` reports both `fn[main]` and `fn[main]/fn[nested]`.
  - A plain-text line (`notes.txt:3`) is added as a `line@…` node.
  - Repeating a call reports `unchanged` and leaves the file byte-identical.
  - Rejected locations leave the record unchanged: a doc-comment line (`src/main.rs:3`), a blank line (`notes.txt:2`), a non-numeric line (`src/main.rs:x`) and a missing file (`missing.rs:1`). The first of these also has its exact error message asserted.
  - Stored inputs equal `outline_input` results.
  - The hash ignores a citation comment but changes with doc-comment edits.
- `add_input_requires_one_target_and_mode_and_resets_changed_records`:
  - Exactly one target and one mode are enforced.
  - Unknown or wrong-kind targets are rejected before anything is written.
  - A changed source produces `refreshed`, updating the existing input in place at the right position.
  - A review reset follows a changed input.
- `add_input_external_sources_respect_allow_and_disallow`: an external file is stored under its absolute path when allowed, and the command fails without modifying the record when the file is disallowed.

**Minor gaps.** Multi-line declarations where the name is on a later line than the node start are not tested explicitly, and the tests exercise only the Rust and plain-text profiles. The shared `declaration_line` logic covers these cases, so I don't think they are a meaningful gap.

text: :::{req} add_input_item
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line containing its name; an anonymous node is declared on the
line where it starts. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
